info.title: PostGrip Worker API
info.description: Tenant-scoped worker inventory, diagnostics, jobs, logs, and controlled lifecycle operations.

post.summary: Create a pending Worker with client-owned bootstrap material
post.description: The caller must durably store the write-only bootstrap values and Idempotency-Key before sending this request. The response never returns either bootstrap value. Public Worker creation is enabled per tenant: a tenant it is not enabled for gets `404` `CAPABILITY_NOT_ENABLED`. Bootstrap values that already registered a Worker (an enrollment key of the organization, or an attestation bootstrap token of any organization) answer `409` `BOOTSTRAP_MATERIAL_REUSED` with nothing written, and release the Idempotency-Key: generate new values and resend.

delete.description: Removes the Worker as the console's Remove Worker dialog does, after confirming that the removal impact is still the one you read. Send `getWorkerRemovalImpact`'s `etag` as `If-Match`; without one the request answers `428` `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`. The removal holds the Worker and reads its impact again before it deletes anything: an impact that has changed since, or an `If-Match` of `*`, answers `412` `PRECONDITION_FAILED` and nothing is changed; read the impact again and decide again. In one transaction the removal deletes the Worker's services and its exclusive deploy projects, unassigns the kept projects' environments from it, clears it as a project default, and deletes or retires the Worker. A Worker that has enrolled keeps its record, marked removed, until its next heartbeat tells its container and attestation signer to stop (`shutdownRequested: true`); the record is deleted 24 hours later. A Worker that never enrolled is deleted at once. After the commit PostGrip removes what the Worker held of those services, their deploy domains and their repository and enterprise runner credentials from the Worker, counted in `workerCleanup`; a revoked or replaced Worker is sent nothing, and those cleanups are counted `skipped`. The Worker host keeps its Docker volumes and Cloudflared; delete the host yourself. A Worker with any managed volume, a lost Worker's unreachable ones included, answers `409` `WORKER_HAS_MANAGED_VOLUMES` and nothing is changed. The request takes no body: one answers `400` `INVALID_BODY`. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. A failed step answers `500` `DB_ERROR` with everything rolled back. Audited as `delete_worker`, with the token as the actor. Every answer but `408`, `429`, `502`, `503` and `504` is kept for the Idempotency-Key for 24 hours, refusals included: a resend with the same key replays it with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and never removes twice. The key does not cover `If-Match`, so after a refusal send the removal again with a new key.

409.description: Conflict. `WORKER_HAS_MANAGED_VOLUMES`: the Worker still owns managed volumes; delete or move them, read the removal impact again and send the removal with a new Idempotency-Key. Nothing is changed. `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` also use this status.

412.description: `PRECONDITION_FAILED`: the removal impact has changed since the one `If-Match` names. Nothing is changed; read the impact again.

get.description: What removing the Worker would delete or change, the read `removeWorker` confirms. `serviceCount` services (targets) on the Worker are deleted with it. Each of `projects` has an environment on the Worker or the Worker as its default: an `exclusive` project, whose every environment assigned a Worker is on this one, is deleted; any other is kept, its environments on the Worker are unassigned, and a `usesAsDefault` project's default Worker is cleared. A Worker with `managedVolumeCount` above zero cannot be removed until its managed volumes are deleted or moved; `unreachableVolumes` are those of a lost Worker, still counted, which only the console's Remove Worker dialog can abandon. The `ETag` header, equal to the body's `etag`, is the impact's fence: send it as `If-Match` with `removeWorker`. It changes when what the removal would do changes, including when a Worker becomes lost; it does not change when a project is renamed, and it does not expire. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. Read-only and not audited.

ETag.description: The removal impact's fence, equal to the body's `etag`: send it as `If-Match` with `removeWorker`.

post.description: PostGrip asks the Worker to re-attest, then computes the check result from its own records: the Worker's trust record and the attestation the orchestrator verified and recorded while the check ran. The Worker's answer only signals that its attempt finished; nothing in it reaches the result or the audit record.

get.description: Requires a Worker that advertises the `log_cursor_v1` capability: an older Worker answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. An invalid `window` or `since` answers `400` `VALIDATION`.

Requires a Worker that advertises the `log_cursor_v1` capability: an older Worker answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. An invalid `window` or `since` answers `400` `VALIDATION`.

post.description: A quarantined or revoked Worker is not placed in maintenance: the request answers `409` `LIFECYCLE_CONFLICT` with `details.status`.

A revoked worker is never resumed: revoked is terminal, so the request changes nothing and answers 409 WORKER_REVOKED. Enroll a new worker or replace the revoked one instead. The refusal is permanent, so a retry with the same Idempotency-Key replays it. Any other Worker that is not in maintenance answers `409` `LIFECYCLE_CONFLICT` with `details.status`.

get.description: The Worker's snapshot schedule and its last run, as PostGrip projects them. Answered when snapshots are off, with `enabled: false`. `degraded` is true when the last snapshot succeeded without capturing everything; `lastSkipped` says what, by kind. `lastExcluded` lists what it left out by the settings' choice, such as the volumes of worker-managed databases with `volumesEnabled` off; that does not make it degraded. `lastRunFailed` and `settingsRejected` report that the last run failed and that saved settings are not in effect; the Worker's error text is not answered. `recovery` is the Worker's restore report when it was recovered from another Worker's archive. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. A pending or revoked Worker, or one the fence finds replaced, revoked or removed, answers `409` `WORKER_NOT_LIVE` with `details.status`. A Worker that doesn't advertise the `worker_snapshot_api_v1` capability answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. Nothing is sent to the Worker for these. A Worker that doesn't answer is `502` `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, any answer outside the operation's own is `502` `WORKER_REFUSED`, and a malformed or oversized one is `502` `INVALID_WORKER_RESPONSE`. The Worker's own messages are never answered.

The Worker's archives in its storage destination, newest first; at most what its retention keeps. Not paged. Snapshots that are off answer `409` `SNAPSHOTS_DISABLED`, and a listing the Worker could not read `502` `SNAPSHOT_LIST_FAILED`. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. A pending or revoked Worker, or one the fence finds replaced, revoked or removed, answers `409` `WORKER_NOT_LIVE` with `details.status`. A Worker that doesn't advertise the `worker_snapshot_api_v1` capability answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. Nothing is sent to the Worker for these. A Worker that doesn't answer is `502` `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, any answer outside the operation's own is `502` `WORKER_REFUSED`, and a malformed or oversized one is `502` `INVALID_WORKER_RESPONSE`. The Worker's own messages are never answered.

post.description: Runs a snapshot on the Worker and waits for it, at most 5 minutes; the Worker keeps running one that takes longer. `snapshot.degraded` and `snapshot.skipped` report anything the archive could not capture. `snapshot.excluded` reports what it left out by the settings' choice, which is not degraded. Snapshots that are off answer `409` `SNAPSHOTS_DISABLED`; a run already in progress `409` `SNAPSHOT_IN_PROGRESS` with `Retry-After`; a failed run `502` `SNAPSHOT_FAILED`; and a run that outlives the wait `504` `SNAPSHOT_UNCONFIRMED`: it may still land, so read the snapshot status before resending. A resend after a `502` or `504` takes another snapshot. Audited as `snapshot_worker`. `WORKER_NOT_LIVE`, `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, `SNAPSHOTS_DISABLED` and `SNAPSHOT_IN_PROGRESS` release the Idempotency-Key, so a resend after the cause is fixed runs again; a completed answer replays with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. A pending or revoked Worker, or one the fence finds replaced, revoked or removed, answers `409` `WORKER_NOT_LIVE` with `details.status`. A Worker that doesn't advertise the `worker_snapshot_api_v1` capability answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. Nothing is sent to the Worker for these. A Worker that doesn't answer is `502` `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, any answer outside the operation's own is `502` `WORKER_REFUSED`, and a malformed or oversized one is `502` `INVALID_WORKER_RESPONSE`. The Worker's own messages are never answered.

get.description: The Worker's snapshot settings. The signing key is never answered: `hasSigningKey` says whether one is stored, and `signerPublicKey` is its public half. Destination credentials are not part of the settings. A settings store the Worker can't read answers `502` `SNAPSHOT_SETTINGS_UNAVAILABLE`. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. A pending or revoked Worker, or one the fence finds replaced, revoked or removed, answers `409` `WORKER_NOT_LIVE` with `details.status`. A Worker that doesn't advertise the `worker_snapshot_api_v1` capability answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. Nothing is sent to the Worker for these. A Worker that doesn't answer is `502` `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, any answer outside the operation's own is `502` `WORKER_REFUSED`, and a malformed or oversized one is `502` `INVALID_WORKER_RESPONSE`. The Worker's own messages are never answered.

put.description: Replaces the whole settings record: every field but `enabled` takes its zero value when omitted, so read the settings and send them back to change one field. `storageDestinationId` names a storage destination of the organization, required to enable snapshots; the bucket coordinates come from that destination, and its credentials must already be delivered to the Worker from the console's Storage page. `signingKey` is write-only: omit it to keep the stored key. Unknown fields answer `400` `INVALID_BODY`; a destination the organization doesn't have, a missing `enabled`, a `retentionCount` below 1 with `enabled` (refused before the Worker is contacted) or settings the Worker refuses answer `400` `VALIDATION`. `details.field`, where one is known, is one of `enabled`, `storageDestinationId`, `cron`, `retentionCount`, `volumeMaxBytes`, `recipientPublicKey` or `signingKey`, and `message` is PostGrip's own text for it. A Worker refusal names its field when the Worker reports one: `storageDestinationId` also covers the destination's bucket settings, which come from the destination. A Worker too old to report one answers without `details.field`. The write is unconditional: no precondition is taken. Answers the settings as the Worker then reads them. Audited as `configure_worker_snapshots`, never with the signing key. `WORKER_NOT_LIVE`, `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, `SNAPSHOTS_DISABLED` and `SNAPSHOT_IN_PROGRESS` release the Idempotency-Key, so a resend after the cause is fixed runs again; a completed answer replays with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A Worker the tenant doesn't have, or a removed one, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. A pending or revoked Worker, or one the fence finds replaced, revoked or removed, answers `409` `WORKER_NOT_LIVE` with `details.status`. A Worker that doesn't advertise the `worker_snapshot_api_v1` capability answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`; upgrade it and retry. Nothing is sent to the Worker for these. A Worker that doesn't answer is `502` `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, any answer outside the operation's own is `502` `WORKER_REFUSED`, and a malformed or oversized one is `502` `INVALID_WORKER_RESPONSE`. The Worker's own messages are never answered.

get.description: The organization's storage destinations, ordered by name: the buckets a Worker's snapshots can go to. Use a destination's `id` as `storageDestinationId` in `updateWorkerSnapshotSettings`. Not paged. The answer holds no credential: a destination's access key and secret stay on the Workers that use it, and which Workers hold them is not answered. Adding a destination and delivering its credentials is done on the console's Storage page.

postgripToken.description: Tenant-scoped PostGrip management token carrying concrete Agent, Worker, and Service grants.

LogWindow.description: How far back to read, as a Go duration greater than 0 and at most `24h`, for example `15m`. Ignored when `since` is sent.
LogWindow.name: window

LogSince.description: Read events from this RFC 3339 instant. It must be within the last 24 hours and at most 5 minutes ahead of the server clock. Takes precedence over `window`.
LogSince.name: since

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The `etag` of the Worker's removal impact (`getWorkerRemovalImpact`).

name.description: At most 128 bytes of UTF-8, with no leading or trailing whitespace and no control characters.

host.description: The Worker's public origin: an absolute https URL with a hostname and optional port, and no credentials, path, query, fragment or IPv6 zone. A single trailing `/` is accepted and removed, and the scheme is stored in lower case; the hostname is kept as sent. An IP literal in a private, loopback or link-local range is refused. The hostname does not have to resolve yet, and another Worker may have the same host.
The Worker's public origin as PostGrip stored it: the scheme in lower case and no trailing `/`.

trustReason.description: Why PostGrip trusts the Worker's attestation or does not. Absent until PostGrip has made an attestation decision for the Worker, while `trustState` is `unknown`.

signerIdentity.description: The attestation signer. On the `createWorker` answer, the signer identity the new Worker's signer must present, `worker-signer:{workerId}`. On reads, the signer of the attestation PostGrip last trusted; absent until PostGrip has trusted one.

recoveredFromWorkerId.description: The identifier of the Worker this one was recovered from, as the Worker reports it.

trustState.description: The Worker's trust state as PostGrip records it after the check.

reason.description: A server-owned code: ATTESTATION_TRUSTED (a fresh attestation was accepted and the Worker is trusted), ATTESTATION_ACCEPTED_UNENFORCED (a fresh attestation was accepted but trust is not enforced), ATTESTATION_REJECTED (a fresh attestation was rejected) or ATTESTATION_NOT_OBSERVED (no new attestation was recorded during the check). Treat any other value as unknown.

wouldTrust.description: True only when PostGrip recorded a fresh attestation it accepted during the check.

attestationExpiresAt.description: When the accepted attestation expires. Present only when wouldTrust is true.

exclusive.description: Every environment of the project that is assigned a Worker is on this one: the removal deletes the project. Otherwise it is kept and its environments on this Worker are unassigned.

usesAsDefault.description: The Worker is the project's default; the removal clears it.

etag.description: The impact's fence, equal to the `ETag` header: send it as `If-Match` with `removeWorker`.

serviceCount.description: Services (targets) on the Worker; the removal deletes them.

managedVolumeCount.description: The Worker's managed volumes that are not abandoned. Any refuses the removal (`409` `WORKER_HAS_MANAGED_VOLUMES`).

unreachableVolumes.description: Those of a lost Worker's managed volumes that it can never act on again, counted in `managedVolumeCount`. Only the console can abandon them.

projects.description: Deploy projects with an environment on the Worker or the Worker as their default, in creation order.

failed.description: Cleanups the Worker refused or did not answer; what they were removing stays on the host.

skipped.description: Cleanups never sent, because the Worker could not be reached (revoked, replaced, or without a host).

shutdownRequested.description: `true`: the Worker had enrolled, so its record is kept, marked removed, until its next heartbeat tells its container and attestation signer to stop, and is deleted 24 hours later. `false`: the record was deleted at once.

keptProjectCount.description: Deploy projects kept because they also run on other Workers.

unassignedEnvironmentCount.description: Environments of kept projects unassigned from the Worker.

clearedProjectDefaultCount.description: Projects whose default Worker was cleared.

WorkerSnapshotSkippedItem.description: Something a snapshot could not capture. Its path and reason stay with the Worker.

targetId.description: The target whose database was not captured, for `sqlite`.

WorkerSnapshotExcludedItem.description: Something a snapshot left out because the Worker's settings chose to: with `volumesEnabled` off, the volume of each worker-managed database (`volume`, with the database's `targetId`). A recovery brings back that database's configuration, not its data. Unlike a skipped item, it does not make the snapshot `degraded`. The volume's name stays with the Worker.

targetId.description: The worker-managed database whose volume was left out, for `volume`.

snapshotId.description: The sortable capture time that names the archive.

objectKey.description: The archive's key in the storage destination; a replacement Worker restores it by this key.
Absent when the Worker could not name the uploaded archive; read the status's `lastSnapshot`.

degraded.description: True when the archive could not capture everything; `skipped` says what.

excluded.description: What the archive left out by the settings' choice; it does not make the snapshot `degraded`.

WorkerSnapshotOrphan.description: An assignment PostGrip holds for the Worker that the recovery restored no state for.

WorkerSnapshotRecovery.description: The restore report of a Worker recovered from another Worker's archive.

anyAgeOverride.description: The latest archive was restored with no age bound.

skippedRecords.description: Records the archive carried that the restore deliberately did not write, by store.

cron.description: The schedule, when snapshots are on.

retention.description: How many archives the Worker keeps, when snapshots are on.

lastRunFailed.description: The last run failed. The Worker's error is not answered; the console and the Worker's logs keep it.

settingsRejected.description: Saved settings could not be applied and are not in effect.

degraded.description: The last snapshot succeeded without capturing everything.

lastExcluded.description: What the last snapshot left out by the settings' choice, such as the volumes of worker-managed databases with `volumesEnabled` off; it does not make the status `degraded`.

WorkerSnapshotSettings.description: A Worker's snapshot settings. The signing key and destination credentials are never answered; the signing key's public half is, as `signerPublicKey`.

provider.description: The destination's provider, as the Worker cached it from the destination.

recipientPublicKey.description: The recovery key's public half; archives are sealed to it.

hasSigningKey.description: Whether a signing key is stored. The key itself is never answered.

signerPublicKey.description: The public half of the stored signing key, standard base64 of an Ed25519 public key, as the Worker derives it; absent when no signing key is stored. It is not a secret. Record it when you set the signing key: a recovery takes it as `WORKER_RECOVERY_SIGNER_PUBLIC_KEY` to pin which archives it accepts, and the copy you recorded, not one read from the Worker at recovery time, is the trust anchor.

storageDestinationId.description: A storage destination of the organization; required when `enabled`.

cron.description: A standard five-field cron schedule, at most 1,024 bytes.

retentionCount.description: How many archives to keep, 1 to 1000 when `enabled`.

recipientPublicKey.description: The recovery key's base64 X25519 public half, at most 1,024 bytes; required when `enabled`.

signingKey.description: The base64 Ed25519 signing seed, at most 1,024 bytes. Write-only: omit it, or send it blank, to keep the stored key. Required when `enabled` and none is stored.

StorageDestination.description: A named bucket the organization's Workers can write snapshots to. It carries no credential: the access key and secret stay on the Workers.

id.description: The destination's id; `updateWorkerSnapshotSettings` takes it as `storageDestinationId`.

name.description: The name shown on the Storage page.

provider.description: `s3` for Amazon S3, `r2` for Cloudflare R2.

region.description: The bucket's region; absent when none is set. Always set for `s3`.

endpoint.description: The S3-compatible endpoint; absent when none is set. Always set for `r2`.

accountId.description: The Cloudflare account id of an `r2` destination; absent when none is set.

prefix.description: The key prefix objects are written under; absent when none is set.
